newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly up on Argentina, cold woes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly up on Argentina, cold woes.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed but mostly higher on concern about the extent of losses to Argentina's wheat crop and on cold weather in the U.S. winter wheat growing region, traders said.
"It was up on uncertainty in Argentina, fund buying and the cold weather," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Recent heavy rainfall in Argentina destroyed nearly one half million acres of wheat and harmed the quality of up to one million tonnes, an Argentine government official said.
But a grain trade source in Buenos Aires disagreed.
The source said USDA showed nearly 1.3 million acres of wheat suffered some damage to quality and that under 200,000 tonnes of wheat was lost.

Exporters in Buenos Aires were irritated by the damage estimates. "Sincerely I think it is the most ridiculous thing I have heard for ages," one exporter said. "There is damage but there is not that much damage." He said the USDA figures sounded closer to the truth.
Dec closed lower on liquidation before expiration.
Wheat closed seven cents per bushel higher to 2-1/2 lower, with Dec down 2-1/2 at $4.02 and March up 6-1/2 at $4.00-3/4.
Traders said the key reason December ran counter to the other contracts and ended lower was long liquidation, tied to position squaring, before expiration of that month slated for 1201 CST Thursday.

Fund buying was very active in the March and estimated at 20 million bushels at least. R.J. O'Brien bought five million March, Tenco Inc and Dean Witter Reynolds each bought two million March and Prudential Securities bought three million bushels of March, traders said.

Traders said the cold weather in the U.S. and some outlooks for the cold snap to continue could harm some of the U.S. winter wheat crop. Also the cold weather was slowing movement of wheat and cash basis markets were firmer.

Technicians said the close below $4.02-1/2 per bushel in the March was disappointing to bulls. "There was a lot of fund buying but it wasn't able to close through $4.02-1/2. I don't know what means for sure it it would have looked better on charts had it closed above $4.02-1/2," a trader said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 25,000 contracts, above the 12,414 traded Tuesday.
In wheat options, Smith Barney sold 1,500 May $3.60 puts at 11-1/2 to 12 cents and Produce Grain bought 800 March $3.60 putss at 3-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, above the 6,847 traded Tuesday.
